lines.text: Study compromised. Cancel return flight.
No one was *coming.*
Two people. One person's supplies. And no ship.
Water: thirty-one percent.
At that rate, the water would be gone around day three sixty-five. Maybe before.
Mara wanted to open envelope twelve. Now.
I said: never early.
We argued for days. Out loud. It felt strange to have someone to argue with.
Day two hundred seventy. Envelope nine.
If they cancel the flight, open twelve. Don't wait.
Hale saw it coming.
He knew they would leave us.
So we opened envelope twelve.
Sam, Mara. The leak was fake. The gauges are fake.
Larkspur Orbital calls it Project SOLO. Two people, each told they're alone, for one year.
I was ordered to write your rules. I wrote rule two so you'd find each other.
If they leave you up there, call one-four-five point eight at night, when you pass over Chile. My daughter listens.
We built an antenna from a cable and a handrail, and plugged it into the station's old ham radio.
We could only reach Chile for about ten minutes, when we flew over it.
Ten minutes. Then Chile slid behind the curve of the Earth, and we waited for the next pass.
Pass after pass. Static.
Thirty passes. Nothing but static.
Day three hundred. The night pass over Chile.
Static. And then, a voice.
Larkspur? My father told me to listen for you.
But that station is empty. It burns up in sixty days.
